concept.title: The Projects page
concept.shortdesc: When you sign in, OpenV opens Home: the Projects page of the active workspace, which brings everything in it together. Home is at the top of the rail on every page.

ul.li: Along the top are the workspace's figures: how many artifacts its projects hold, the share of their requirements that are traced (a test case verifies them) and verified, and how many test cases fail.

Needs you lists what waits on you across every project, each line naming its project: artifacts in review to approve, suspect links to confirm, test runs in progress, failing test cases and comments you have not read (never your own). Click a line to open the artifact it names (for a link, the artifact the link starts from). The button on the right says what it does: Review and Open open the artifact, Continue the test run. A suspect link has two buttons instead: ✓ confirms that the link still holds, and ✗ removes the link once you confirm it. Either way the line leaves the list there and then. A comment has Mark read, which takes every unread comment on that artifact off the list without opening it, and Mark all read, in the panel's header, clears every comment at once. Each leaves a line saying what was marked, with Undo to put it back. Review all, in the panel's header, opens the review queue of the project with the most waiting.

Activity shows the newest events across the workspace's projects, who did what to which artifact. Click an event to open what it is about: the artifact, a link's source artifact, the board, the agent run, the test run, the baseline, or a comment with its notes open. A deleted artifact has nowhere to go, so its event is not a link. When agents have proposed changes, a card below it counts the proposals waiting.

Projects, below them, is where you pick a project, and + New project in its header starts one. Each row shows the project's name and how many artifacts it holds, a one-line description, and two bars: the share of its requirements that are traced (a test case or a manual verification stands behind them) and the share verified (their tests pass, or they are verified by hand). A project with no requirements yet says so instead. The project you opened last is marked with a blue edge. Each row carries its action buttons:

strow.stentry: Save as template — snapshot this project as a reusable template
Edit project — rename it or change the description
Download — opens the download wizard (format, sections, attachments)
Delete project — removes the project and all its artifacts

conbody.p: Click anywhere else on the row to open the project.

On a computer or tablet, Home fits the window: the page itself does not scroll. Needs you, Activity and Projects share the height below the figures, and each scrolls on its own when it has more than fits, so Needs you lists everything waiting rather than the first few. A very short window, or a form open below the list, scrolls the page as before.
